name: יִשְׂרָאֵל
gloss: he strives with God (and prevails); or God strives, rules
summary: The name God gave Jacob at Peniel and confirmed at Bethel, and then the name of the people descended from him, their land and the northern kingdom: about 2,500 uses, among them “the sons of Israel” to whom the feasts of Lev 23 are spoken and “the thousands of Israel” of Num 10. Its letters are יִשְׂרֶה, the he-form imperfect of שָׂרָה “strive, prevail”, with אֵל “God”. The text explains it: “for you have striven with God and with men, and have prevailed” (Gen 32:29), and Hosea retells it with שָׂרָה and then וַיָּשַׂר, the form that elsewhere means “he ruled” (Hos 12:4–5; Jdg 9:22). In names of this shape אֵל is usually the subject (יִשְׁמָעֵאל, “for Yahweh has heard”, Gen 16:11), which would read “God strives” or “God rules”; scripture’s own explanation makes Jacob the one who strove with God.

evidence.note: לֹא יַעֲקֹב יֵאָמֵר עוֹד שִׁמְךָ כִּי אִם־יִשְׂרָאֵל כִּי־שָׂרִיתָ עִם־אֱלֹהִים וְעִם־אֲנָשִׁים וַתּוּכָל: the naming, and its reason.
בְּאוֹנוֹ שָׂרָה אֶת־אֱלֹהִים, in his strength he strove with God: the verb of the name, set against עָקַב, the verb of “Jacob”.
וַיָּשַׂר אֶל־מַלְאָךְ וַיֻּכָל, he strove with (prevailed over) the angel and overcame; he wept and sought his favour.
At Bethel: “your name shall not be called Jacob any more, but Israel shall be your name”, and he called his name Israel.
וַיָּשַׂר אֲבִימֶלֶךְ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵל: Hosea’s form וַיָּשַׂר meaning “ruled”, here over Israel itself.
יִשְׁמָעֵאל, “for Yahweh has heard”: a name of the same shape, God the subject.
Esau on the first name: “is he not rightly named Jacob? for he has supplanted me (וַיַּעְקְבֵנִי)”.
דַּבֵּר אֶל־בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל: the people named after him, to whom Yahweh’s appointed feasts are given.
רָאשֵׁי אַלְפֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל, the heads of the thousands of Israel.
Yahweh has spoken good concerning Israel.
“Return, Yahweh, to the ten thousands of the thousands of Israel.”
וּבְשֵׁם יִשְׂרָאֵל יְכַנֶּה: one will surname himself by the name of Israel.
The Biblical Aramaic יִשְׂרָאֵל: Haggai and Zechariah prophesied in the name of the God of Israel.
“Behold, truly an Israelite, in whom is no deceit”: the name set against Jacob’s deceit (Gen 27:35).
“Not all who are of Israel are Israel.”

note: TIPNR has the man Israel@Gen.25.26 (Jacob), whose record carries the name for the people and the Aramaic form too; it has no separate person record for the nation, so only he is tagged. bdb: u.ce.ab is the Hebrew name (2,514 tokens), xj.ak.ah the Biblical Aramaic. The verb behind it is attested only in Gen 32:29 and Hos 12:4 (with שָׂרַר in Hos 12:5), so the name rests on those verses and on Arabic šariya “persist, contend”. Leads not followed: the Egyptian ysrjꜣr of the Merneptah stele (Wiktionary links it to Israel; not found in the TLA list) and the Moabite stone’s ישראל (compston-1919 has the text; not checked). The name Jeshurun (יְשֻׁרוּן) is from ישׁר, not this root.
